report.tagline: A UK payments company that lets businesses pull recurring and one-off payments straight from customers' bank accounts, instead of using cards.
report.simpleSummary: GoCardless helps businesses collect money directly from their customers' bank accounts. Think of a gym, a software company or a utility that bills you every month: instead of charging your card, they use GoCardless to take a Direct Debit from your bank. It is cheaper than cards, and payments do not fail when a card expires. In 2026 it was bought by Mollie, a Dutch payments company.

keyNumbers.label: Revenue FY25
keyNumbers.note: Companies House accounts for the year to June 2025, reported by Tech.eu. Up about 18% from £131.3 million. GoCardless's own release said 22% growth on its measure.

keyNumbers.label: Loss FY25
keyNumbers.note: Tech.eu, down from £33.6 million. First quarter with positive adjusted EBITDA came in late 2025, and it expected its first adjusted EBITDA positive year in FY26.

keyNumbers.label: Payment volume FY25
keyNumbers.note: Tech.eu. About double the year before, helped by buying the open banking firm Nuapay.

keyNumbers.label: Sale to Mollie
keyNumbers.note: Announced December 2025, completed September 2026 (Crowdfund Insider). Below its 2022 private valuation of about $2.1 billion.

overview.whatItDoes: GoCardless runs bank-to-bank payments for businesses. It handles Direct Debit in the UK and similar schemes in Europe, the US, Australia and more, plus instant open banking payments. Businesses connect through its dashboard, billing software like Xero, or an API. It charges a small fee per payment.
howItWorks: A business sends its customer a GoCardless payment page or adds it to its checkout.
The customer enters bank details once and agrees a mandate, which is permission for the business to collect payments.
Each billing date, GoCardless pulls the payment from the customer's bank through the local bank scheme, like Bacs in the UK or SEPA in Europe.
Money settles to the business a few days later, minus GoCardless's fee.
Success+ uses data from millions of payments to retry failed ones at the best time.
Instant Bank Pay uses open banking to take one-off payments instantly, without a card.
overview.valueProposition: Collect recurring payments cheaply and reliably, without card expiry, high card fees or chasing customers.

businessModel.summary: GoCardless makes money by charging a small fee on each payment it collects, plus paid add-ons like smart retries and fraud tools. Its costs are bank scheme fees, fraud losses and staff.

revenueStreams.detail: A percentage plus a fixed amount, often capped, for each payment collected.
Success+, Protect+ and other paid features.
Extra fees for collecting in other countries and converting currency.
Custom pricing for large businesses and software partners.

businessModel.pricing: UK standard plan has been about 1% + 20p per domestic transaction, capped at £4. Higher plans and international payments cost more. Enterprise pricing is custom. Check gocardless.com/pricing for current rates.
costDrivers: Bank scheme fees (Bacs, SEPA and others)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a £50 monthly gym payment. GoCardless charges about 1% + 20p, so 70p. The bank scheme fee is a few pence. Fraud and failure costs might be another few pence. So GoCardless keeps about 50p to 60p of gross profit per payment. A gym with 1,000 members brings about £600 a month of gross profit. The business saves money too: a card might cost it about 1.5% + 20p, or 95p. GoCardless's revenue was about 0.2% of the £79 billion it processed in FY25, because large payments hit the fee cap.

howTheyGetUsers: Integrations in accounting and billing apps like Xero and QuickBooks
Direct sales to large subscription businesses
Search and content around 'Direct Debit for small business'
Now, cross-selling to Mollie's merchants in Europe
whatBringsUsersBack: Recurring payments run automatically every month
Mandates are hard to move to another provider
growth.moat: Once a business has thousands of customer mandates with GoCardless, moving them is risky and slow. Data from millions of payments makes its retry and fraud tools better than a new rival's. It also has connections to bank schemes in many countries.

northStar.metric: Value of payments successfully collected on time for businesses each month
northStar.why: Businesses come to GoCardless to get paid on time. Successful, on-time collections show that value, and they drive revenue. That is what makes it a good north star metric: it moves only when customers get real value.

interviewQuestions.question: Why would a business choose GoCardless over Stripe?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare costs, failure rates, use case (recurring vs one-off) and coverage. Explain when each wins.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase payment success rates?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break failures into causes. Ideas: retries, reminders, timing near payday. Track success and dispute rates.

interviewQuestions.question: After the Mollie deal, how would you integrate the products?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find overlapping customers, quick wins, and risks. Prioritise by revenue and effort.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the health of GoCardless's business?
interviewQuestions.hint: Volume, revenue per payment, merchant churn, success rate, fraud losses. Pick a north star.

interviewQuestions.question: Should GoCardless enter India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Discuss UPI AutoPay and NACH, which already do recurring payments cheaply. Is there room? Who would pay?
